title: DeviceDesiredState
description: Declarative desired-state document that Smplify (the enterprise control plane) sends to a Punar device (spec sections 38, 50). Models the full section 38 example plus the firewall defaults of section 44.4 and the application policy of section 46. This is a YAML configuration manifest: field names are camelCase per the repo naming asymmetry (schemas/README.md); the apiVersion string is validated verbatim.

apiVersion.title: API version
apiVersion.description: Manifest API version, verbatim from spec section 38. Independent of the schema-tree version (schemas/README.md, Versioning).

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Identifies the organization and the device this desired state targets (spec section 38).

organization.title: Organization
organization.description: Organization identifier, e.g. 'acme' (spec sections 38, 47). Kept as a non-empty string: the spec shows a bare slug and defines no organization-id grammar.

spec.title: Desired state spec
spec.description: Desired configuration for the device (spec section 38). All five sections are present in the section 38 example — the only full DeviceDesiredState example — and are therefore required; relaxing a required field later is a compatible change (schemas/README.md, Versioning).

security.title: Security baseline
security.description: Enterprise security baseline settings (spec sections 38, 44). Extensible object: spec section 44.5 says enterprise policy should also govern service controls (SSH, Bluetooth, removable storage, local admin, screen lock, kernel/module restrictions, developer exceptions), so unknown keys are permitted here. Only 'firewall' is required: the section 44.4 declarative example shows a security block containing only 'firewall'.

diskEncryption.title: Disk encryption
diskEncryption.description: Disk-encryption requirement for this device (spec sections 38, 44.2).

required.title: Disk encryption required
required.description: Whether disk encryption is required on this device (spec sections 38, 44.2).

secureBoot.title: Secure Boot
secureBoot.description: Secure Boot requirement for this device (spec sections 38, 44.1).

required.title: Secure Boot required
required.description: Whether Secure Boot is required on this device (spec sections 38, 44.1).

enabled.title: Firewall enabled
enabled.description: Whether the firewall is enabled (spec sections 38, 44.4).

inboundDefault.title: Inbound default verdict
inboundDefault.description: Default verdict for inbound traffic (spec section 44.4). Optional: present in the section 44.4 example, absent from the section 38 example.

outboundDefault.title: Outbound default verdict
outboundDefault.description: Default verdict for outbound traffic (spec section 44.4). Optional: present in the section 44.4 example, absent from the section 38 example.

applications.title: Application policy
applications.description: Application policy (spec sections 38, 46). 'required' appears in both spec examples and is required here; 'denied' and 'allowUserInstall' appear only in the section 46 example and are optional. Strict object: spec section 46 says application semantics should remain stable even if the underlying package system changes.

required.title: Required applications
required.description: Applications that must be installed, by package name (spec sections 38, 46).

items.title: Required application package name
items.description: Package name of an application that must be installed (spec sections 38, 46).

denied.title: Denied applications
denied.description: Applications that must not be installed (spec section 46).

items.title: Denied application entry
items.description: A denied-application entry; the spec section 46 example shows an object with a 'package' field.

package.title: Denied package name
package.description: Package name of an application that must not be installed (spec section 46).

allowUserInstall.title: Allow user installs
allowUserInstall.description: Whether users may install additional applications themselves (spec section 46).

ai.title: AI policy
ai.description: AI configuration for the device (spec section 38). Extensible object: spec section 71 sketches future keys under 'ai' (models, cloudModels, localModels, externalMcp), so unknown keys are permitted here.

policy.title: AI policy name
policy.description: Name of the named AI policy applied to this device, e.g. 'engineering-standard' (spec sections 38, 20).

privateRelay.title: Private relay
privateRelay.description: Native OS-level private relay configuration (spec sections 38, 33).

enabled.title: Private relay enabled
enabled.description: Whether the native private relay is enabled (spec sections 38, 33).

channel.title: Update channel
channel.description: Update channel name, e.g. 'stable' (spec sections 38, 57). Kept as an open non-empty string: section 38 shows only 'stable', and section 57 defines rollout stages, not a channel enum — inventing one would be a speculative narrowing.

firewall_default.title: Firewall default verdict
firewall_default.description: Manifest-local default verdict for a firewall traffic direction: allow or deny (spec section 44.4). Deliberately narrower than the shared runtime 'decision' def — 'approval_required' is not meaningful as a packet default; do not widen.

package_name.title: Package name
package_name.description: Application package name, e.g. 'git', 'podman', '1password', 'tailscale' (spec sections 38, 46). Kept as a non-empty string: the spec pins application semantics, not a package-name grammar (section 46), and tightening later would be a breaking change.
